item.content:encoded:
Deleted an article by TheBeginningIsTheEnd at -15 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description:
SCP-5127 is a parasite that attaches itself to it's victims through ingestion of SCP-5127.
It manifests as a purple mold usually found on items such as fresh vegetables and fruits.
It can multiply and spread throughout entire farms in mere minutes, as it has been enhanced by unknown means to find the quickest way to infect a human body.

Feedback is as follows:

+ Ralliston
– Ralliston

Author, the mainsite is for finished works. This is clearly not finished - it’s lacking an Object Class and Special Containment Procedures. Additionally, this reads a lot like a generic thing which kills you. I suggest you use the ideas critique forums to polish the idea up to give it some depth, the place can be of great help.

Also,

D-Class Test Results
378 D-Class personnel have ingested SCP-5127, each with results varying inbetween the above side-effects.

I highly doubt the Foundation would sacrifice 387 people on such tests.

+ TSATPWTCOTTTADC
– TSATPWTCOTTTADC

Author, take a look at the instructions on the How to Write and SCP guide linked in the sidebar to learn how to give your article a title the right way.

Deleted an article by Agent malcom at -15 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5729 is a cancerous growth located in the upper abdominal area and in 5% of cases brain working as a separate organ, which upon being "activated" by an unknown factor it will manifest into rapid growths forming any of the following: controlable tentacle-like structures, coverage of the arms and/or legs or a violent burst. Upon activation of SCP-5729 the subject from now on named SCP-5729-1 will become highly aggresive attacking every multi-celular organism it encounters.

Feedback is as follows:

+ ItsDenali
– ItsDenali

This feels really short and underdeveloped, and the second breach log being almost entirely redacted doesn't add anything to the article as a whole. Really all you've got here is a thing that does a thing, without much depth to it.

This idea does have potential, but I'd take this back to the Critique Forum and try to develop more points on it, such as what causes it, where it comes from, and what -1 instances' "common goal" is beyond escaping and killing people at random.

Good luck, author.

+ MrAnakinSpecter
– MrAnakinSpecter

Aside from the conceptual feedback (which I second) already given, I would like to add that you might also want to double-check some words if you aren't sure how to spell them, author. Additionally, what I'm assuming are supposed to be black boxes at the end are not showing up for me.

Deleted an article by Douglas Gorde at -13 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5315 is a horse barn found in ████, Michigan. Its dimensions equate to roughly 30’x40’x30’. It is constructed almost entirely from oak and has been painted red with white highlights on supports or moldings, though the paint has chipped and faded due to age. SCP-5315 contains a large, main door, a back door, and a window situated above the main door which could be used to access the loft.

Feedback is as follows:

+ MrAnakinSpecter
– MrAnakinSpecter

30’x40’x30’.

Use metric.

If the main door of SCO-5315

SCP*

This isn't a terrible concept, but I think that the pure descriptive nature of the writing takes away any sort intrigue added by the anomaly.

So this is, for me, the point where the actual story in the article kicks off; before this is just…discovery stuff which is fine but it's not as interesting as exploring what the Foundation does with the camera and that leads me to the big question: what actually happens with this?

Alot of test logs of important historical events (e.g.: life of Jesus Christ) would be part of the article. Most of the importnat information would obviously be blacked out or would require O5 authorisation to access it.

Beyond this, focusing on historical stuff feels like it's squandering the potential a little: it feels like this is a thing the foundation could use to predict future events and in turn, like something the foundation could be tricked by and accidentally cause something horrible to happen but??

item.title: Re: Double Edged
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

However after its use something terrible of equal or greater intensity will happen that will affect the user in some way or form.

This makes this idea feel like a kinda, generic cursed magic item; like, the kinda thing you'd expect to see in a game of DnD, not a SCP. My advice would be really consider what the bad effects are here and how they can be thematically tied together: two similar uses of the sword should feel like they produce two similar outcomes; so that you can setup a feel for the reader of how this works. It might be worth considering whether you can use the effects here to imply something about the sword; like it punishing some people more than others to indicate it has like, preferences in how it's used say.

would be found talking about its creation and its uses, such as a major example the sword being uses by a celt who used the blade to kill an entire army only for a plague to befall his village originating from the corpses that killed the same amount of people the warrior killed

Relying on events that happened a long time ago in your narrative is generally not a great idea: it's a lot harder to get a reader invested in a battle that happened thousands of years ago to characters we can never meet with stakes that have already played out than it is to get a reader invested in a character doing something right now with an uncertain outcome.

At the end of the day, my broad feelings on this is that it really needs you to explore what happens now the Foundation has it: do they use it? do they test it to find out what the limits of its power are? Why does this matter?

Basically: at the end of the day, the PoV this story is told from is The Foundation; and in turn, you need to figure out how to get them involved in the story somehow.

Forum thread: Double Edged

item.title: Re: Fear That Walks
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Central Narrative: none

This is a deal breaker for me. A SCP article is best when it shows why the SCP is interesting and how it's existence affects the world; and … not including that section generally leads to a boring SCP article.

In particular: this is a SCP that feeds off fear, which is fine but perhaps it's overbroad; but that feeding is most effective when you setup a scenario where someone/a group of people can experience the fear and react. Like, considered say, Friday the 13th: it works as a film because it's not just all "hey what's up my name's jason, i kill people" but because there's actual characters who can react to jason trying to kill them and try to survive and succeed/fail; and this tension is what makes it interesting. If you want this SCP to work, you're going to have to figure out how you can achieve something like that within the SCP format; or alternatively, figure out a different emotion to tap into: perhaps this thing feeds off fear and the story is really the foundation using that to make their employees have less fear overall and in turn exploring what that causes to happen.

I would strongly urge you to narrow down what the SCP can do a lot more than you have: if the SCP can basically do anything that can cause fear, then a reader finds it a lot harder to emphasise with the plight of the characters because the SCP can just…break any rule it wants to to scare them? But if it's like, constrained into one physical body, we can have expectations for where stuff is safe (e.g. a locked room with no entrances) and in turn have that expectation broken to generate even more horror.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Fear That Walks

item.title: Re: the weight of the world on your shoulders
item.content:encoded:
the main article is based around the perspective of a researcher assigned to log the current events taking place.

so like…what are the current events taking place?

My view here is that there's definitely like an interesting story in a world winding down and coming to an end, and putting up a final note about how everything has ended; but my concern here is that you don't really have much narratively to bridge 'is something happening' to 'we know what's happening and can't stop it' to 'the world has ended': it feels like this needs some kind of desperate plan to save earth that doesn't work, or focussed in story about a person wrapping up their life before the end, or just…something to happen y'know?

item.title: Re: A 4th degree burn
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Keter level scp, when humans sustain burns of incredibly high temperatures, their nervous systems re-wire to survive in intense heat. They turn into vaguely humanoid personages of flame who can't talk and can only live in intense heat.

For clarity: is there a thing that causes this? Or does this just happen to anyone exposed to really hot flame? If it's the second, why is it considered anomalous instead of a natural process?

The narrative would follow the foundation containing several instances of this scp after a failed rocket launch in South Korea. After losing several instances due to decreasing temperatures, they are able to create a containment chamber with a increased temperature so then the final instance could be contained.

My concern with this is it feels like all the instances they initially contain would be contained at the same time; so it feels like if the instances cool down enough to start dying, they'd all end up dying at roughly the same time without there being time for the foundation to a) figure out how to solve this b) actually build a sufficiently hot containment chamber

The foundation can recreate this and they roast a D-class and make another instance. They then cool down the chamber and discover the temperature they "die" at.

My concern is that a) this feels cruel and out of character for the foundation a little b) this just doesn't feel interesting; it's…information dumping about the SCP but not in a way that really adds much? Like why does it matter to me, the reader, what temperature they die at? If it's 800C or 1000C or 1200C, what changes?

Basically it's the fear of literally burning forever. A literal hell.

See this bit feels nicely evocative but my concern is that it's going to be really hard to show this in an interesting way: you're effectively constrained to just having an instance complain a lot about the pain, which isn't like…a good way to get a reader to care?

If I was to summarise my feelings on this, it'd be that it's an interesting concept but it feels like it really needs something more interesting to be done with it for it to work as a SCP to me. I think exploring the pain is a good idea but I think it has to end up going somewhere: either the Foundation tries to figure out how to stop the pain, or there's a big ethical debate about whether it's okay to keep the scp alive if it's in constant pain, and in turn this debate needs to be resolved somehow.

item.title: Re: Need help on an idea that I've already drafted -296 words
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

There's something hidden lurking in this tape, and it's starting to wake up.

So like…this is your entire central narrative but it reads more like you writing the blurb for a book than pitching the idea to me. What's hidden? Why is it waking up? What does it waking up cause to happen? Why does this matter to a reader? Bear in mind: it's a bad idea to worry about spoilers here. If a reviewer can't see the full extent of your idea, they can't judge whether it's good or not.

I'm really looking to see a rough plot outline here tying e.g. how the progression of the tape waking up happens to elements of the SCP article you're intending to write.

At the moment, I don't really know enough about the idea to have a feel for what's happening or why it's interesting; and so I can't really provide much input. The compulsive effect that causes folk to run away feels dicey but it feels like it could be easily explained as a non-compulsive effect caused by whatever's on the tape being horrifying. Though, if you do this, you'll need to show it: a character reacting in fear is a lot more effective at eliciting fear than a dispassionate description saying that's what happens, y'know?

Hey there ragewhatle17, I'll be critting your idea today!
This is going to be a brief crit, so here goes:

I'm going to stop you right here and tell you SCP-173 did it better. This is a statue that kills people when it can't be observed (i.e lack of visible light), and people will tear this apart for that reason if it ever ends up on-Site.
My advice? Don't continue with this idea, and I'd advise you to scrap any similar ideas you may have. As a general rule, statues that move when not looked at (or in this case, when not in an illuminated area) are a bad idea on this Site.
I'd recommend checking out the Guide Hub for some great essays to help you with future ideas.

That's it for my crit. Hope it helps!

item.title: Re: Insights of insanity
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback! I'll try to explain my vision for the origin of the book a bit better, as well as dive into the dreamer. This can be a bit long of an explanation, so bear with me.

+ show
- hide

Let's start with the origin. The book comes from a scientific "cult" whose purpose was trying to gain a deeper understanding of the workings of the universe. They started experimenting on eachother/victims to gain this understanding. They believed that by altering their bodies through anomalous means, they could also alter their mind to gain a deeper understanding of the universe. They experimented with eyes to gain "insight" into the universe. The book's origin was originally just one of the books where they recorded their findings. The foundation found the book after reports of all of the members of the cult disappearing, which sparked their interest. They found the church of the cult, along with a number of bodies from members, although not all people where found here. The book was also recovered here.

Now onto the dreamer. This comes from the believe the cult holds, after their experiments. They believe that there is an entity, they call the dreamer. The dreamer is an entity beyond our understanding, who is constantly experiencing dreams. The cult believes that our universe is just one of these dreams, and when the entity wakes up, our reality will cease to be, only to be replaced by a new dream. They believe this has happened before, and will happen again. The dreamer isn't aware of the fact that this is a dream. The cult believes that nobody is an individual, but they're all just fragments of the dreamer, unaware of their greater connection to him. So everyone is just a small part of the dreamer, but they don't know of it. The cult believes that by "rebuilding" their connection to the dreamer, they can gain even deeper insights into the universe. The problem is, to rebuild this connection, they have to accept that they aren't an individual, and that they aren't even real. They are just a small part of the dreamer. This causes them to lose their sense of self, their individuality. So the more they rebuild their connection, the more insight they gain, the less they are themselves. They lose what made them them, and start adopting mannerisms and ticks of other people around them. Until they have no individuality left, and they simply cease to be.

So the book just helps people believe the insights the cult found, by changing the body of the reader, so their minds are more ready for the things they'll read in the book.


Hope this better showed my vision!

item.title: Re: Night Terrors - Seeking Idea Critique
item.content:encoded:
I have a good idea of what this SCP is, and what she can do, but I need a bit of help figuring out the specifics of her story.

See, the anomaly isn't that interesting. I feel like there's a lot of "little kids that are dangerous without knowing it" on the wiki and in fiction entirely… But what could set you apart is the story. How you characterize the child, the researchers, and how you create an emotional arc (or journey) for the reader to go on.

Honestly, no one is going to be able to help you write this, its something you have to answer for yourself.

Ask yourself the following questions, and then try to answer them by editing the post to reflect your feelings on the answers:

  • Who's perspective is the article from? Who are we going to relate to as readers?
  • Where are the stakes for this narrative? Beyond the fact that there are monsters… what is the intrigue? Only figuring out what is going on with the girl? Is there some way you could up the drama/stakes?
  • What sort of tone are you going for? Is this scary? Is this an emotional story?

Mostly suggest you stay away from vivid descriptions of the abuse the child goes through, unless its super important to the narrative. Shock value is a weak story aspect.

The statue hasn't been in a brighter light other than the torches for a very long time.
The statue was made from a human, the statue's purpose is to be in the spotlight, to entertain and amaze humans. It's not supposed to move because that is not what they are supposed to do, only in the dark they are allowed to move.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP can disrupt electricity which renders light bulbs, flashlights, phones, and even clean energy useless. This makes the SCP harder to contain when light bulbs and spotlights aren't used against the SCP since lights immobilize the object. So the foundation has to use oil lamps, candles, and torches to keep the SCP from breach containment.

item.title: Re: Infinity war but in SCP
item.content:encoded:
Hey there Bawower, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither a particularly experienced nor offical reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let's begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
Wooooosh

Elevator Pitch

So your pitch is some kind of collaboration between all of the major GoIs to stop… something, however tensions arise due to everyone being suspicious of everyone else? At the moment, this seems more like a Tale than an SCP. It it's also ambitious. Very ambitious. This kind of thing would require an immense amount of research and the like to pull off, and I don't know if a new author such as yourself would be skilled enough to execute this effectively. You're also quite vague about what the GoIs are fighting against. What is it?

Central Narrative

An unknown individual that is notably immature sends a threat message to every GoI, and despite having absolutely no evidence whatsoever to back up their claims, every GoI believes them and unites? This, to a relatively knowledgeable member of the Site (which they probably would be, if, hypothetically, they were reading this) would be an immediate shattering of the suspension of disbelief. This simply isn't feasible. You need to come up with a more pressing threat if you want to make this idea reasonable.

Hook/Attention Grabber

That the SCP will unite all of the GoIs, that's a good hook. The next part, which features gratuitous name-dropping of pop culture references (specifically Among Us), isn't. Try to keep away from that if possible.

+ Open General Thoughts +
I don't know about this, buddy

This idea has the potential to work well, but there are some crippling problems. Firstly, this seems more like a Tale than an SCP (but it could still work as an SCP), due to your vagueness on what the anomaly actually is, and much more of the focus on the 'GoI unification' part. Secondly, your vagueness on the anomaly is really shooting you in the foot here. As I have no idea what the anomaly behind this (and thus the whole point of the article) is, I can't really crit it. What I did see I wasn't impressed by due to logistical problems (see above section for detail). Thirdly, if this is based around Avengers: Infinity War (a mediocre movie, in my opinion), then why write about it if we've already seen it? Wouldn't that be plagiarism and/or boring?
To sum up, I personally don't like this idea due to it being incomplete (what is the anomaly?) and how it is unoriginal (a collaboration between all of the GoIs, if based on Infinity War, isn't original).

I'd recommend two things:
1. Checking out the Guide Hub (and more specifically this article, first section) for a whole bunch of great essays full of helpful advice!
2. Reaching out to some reviewers from the Butterfly Squad. They're really helpful and have tonnes of experience!

And finally, to sum up your idea in one sentence1:
A mysterious individual contacts every GoI and threatens them with an anomalous object capable of mass destruction, causing the all of the GoIs to unite to find and fight against the individual.

Anyway, that's it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. This is to help you get a simple summary of the bare bones of your idea that a critter will see. You may find something here that you don't actually like, or find us critters are getting the wrong impression.

item.title: Time Traveling Ice Dispenser
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX represents a an extremely damaged and worn down ice dispensing machine. It was originally discovered by a team of Paleontologists on a expedition within the Bone Valley Formation, Florida, United States in 2018. From here it was reported in scientific literature, and was then taken to the foundation. From here it was kept within a anomalous item storage locker until SCP-XXXX began excreting a dark blue gas from its front.

Central Narrative: This gas designated SCP-XXXX-1 is not immediately dangerous, however once this gas is mixed with Oxygen, it will begin turning the surrounding air cold. Small doses of SCP-XXXX-1 is not harmful however large doses make the surrounding area extremely cold and as a consequence can cause frostbite as well as hyperthermia. Because of SCP-XXXX-1 the foundation wanted to look in the exterior of SCP-XXXX to see how it was producing SCP-XXXX-1 on an almost infinite level. However when looking inside of SCP-XXXX they discovered a small metal box witch contained two written notes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: These notes were signed by Dr. [INSERT NAME HERE] as well having the dates on them, which were months ahead of the current date. The first of these was a copy of an updated page of SCP-XXXX with a stick it note saying "Might come in handy". The second is a warning stating how the author of the note Dr. [INSERT NAME HERE] is concerned about the foundation accessing the core of SCP-XXXX due to the possibility that SCP-XXXX-1 could flow infinitely out of SCP-XXXX leaving the audience on a cliffhanger.

Additional Notes:So the first part of the page will just be the usual Special containment procedures, description as well as an added discovery page. Next will be a warning stating only level 4 and over clearance is needed to access, once readers access they will learn about how it was originally kept in a items locker, SCP-XXXX-1 as well as the notes.
